title: Build and protect a controlling focus
instructions: Continue from the E6.3 plan. The school-learned method is breaking a large task into smaller parts. The example is a charity sale: first divide publicity, supplies, prices and staffing; then use the same method to adapt when rain moves the stalls indoors. Answer all six questions about writing and maintaining one controlling focus.

parts.prompt: Which sentence is the clearest controlling focus?

options.text: Mathematics is one of the subjects taught at school.
Breaking a large task into smaller parts is useful beyond mathematics because it makes a complicated event manageable and helps me adapt when plans change.
The charity sale had food, posters, tables and many visitors.
Organisation always guarantees perfect results in every situation.

choice_rationales.A: This states a general fact but does not answer how the learning transfers or matters.
choice_rationales.B: This names the learned method, its application beyond mathematics and the insight both planned paragraphs can prove.
choice_rationales.C: This lists event details without explaining the transferred school learning.
choice_rationales.D: This absolute promise is stronger than the example can support.

parts.hint: Choose the sentence that identifies the learning, application and main insight without overclaiming.
parts.correct_explanation: The complete focus gives both body paragraphs one centre: the method makes the event manageable and supports adaptation.

parts.prompt: Which THREE features make that controlling focus effective?

options.text: It identifies the school-learned method.
It shows an application beyond the original mathematics setting.
It states the main effect that the example will demonstrate.
It promises that the method can never fail.
It introduces several unrelated school skills.

choice_rationales.A: The central learning must remain identifiable throughout the composition.
choice_rationales.B: Transfer to another area of life is a required part of the task contract.
choice_rationales.C: The manageable-task and adaptation insight gives the evidence a purpose.
choice_rationales.D: An absolute guarantee would be an unsupported overclaim.
choice_rationales.E: Multiple unrelated skills would split the focus.

parts.hint: Select the learning, application and insight; reject an absolute promise and a split focus.
parts.correct_explanation: A controlling focus unites what was learned, where it transfers and what the evidence will show.

parts.prompt: Which topic sentence gives the first paragraph a distinct job while advancing the focus?

options.text: Before the sale, dividing the event into four task areas turned a confusing workload into a plan that we could manage.
Breaking a large task into smaller parts is useful beyond mathematics because it is useful.
Teamwork is another completely different lesson that schools teach.
There were many colourful posters near the school hall.

choice_rationales.A: This names the planning stage and explains its new contribution to the manageable-task claim.
choice_rationales.B: This repeats the focus without identifying what the paragraph will add.
choice_rationales.C: This introduces a second central school learning.
choice_rationales.D: The poster detail has no stated relationship to the controlling focus.

parts.hint: The topic sentence should name both the shared method and the paragraph's particular contribution.
parts.correct_explanation: The sentence maintains the method while establishing the first paragraph's job: showing how it created a manageable initial plan.

parts.prompt: Which topic sentence keeps the second paragraph on the same focus?

options.text: When rain changed the venue, working through one urgent part at a time helped us adapt without losing control of the whole event.
Leadership is more important than problem-solving and should become the new topic.
Rain is a type of weather that can happen in many countries.
The sale was certainly the most successful event ever held at the school.

choice_rationales.A: This varies the thread language while showing how the same method supported adaptation.
choice_rationales.B: This switches the central learning and creates a split focus.
choice_rationales.C: This fact does not explain the method's application.
choice_rationales.D: This unsupported claim neither advances nor accurately limits the focus.

parts.hint: Look for the same method applied to the complication, with a new contribution rather than a new central skill.
parts.correct_explanation: The topic sentence connects the rain response to the same step-by-step method and advances the adaptation part of the focus.

parts.prompt: Which sentence is detail drift and should be removed or explicitly reconnected?

options.text: Assigning a deadline to each task made it easier to see what was unfinished.
After the venue changed, we checked the urgent categories before moving less important items.
One poster used orange lettering, and a helper wore new shoes that day.
Handling one priority at a time reduced confusion when the original plan changed.

choice_rationales.A: This detail shows how dividing the task made progress manageable.
choice_rationales.B: This action demonstrates the method during the complication.
choice_rationales.C: These visual details have no explained connection to the learned method or central insight.
choice_rationales.D: This sentence links the action directly to the adaptation claim.

parts.hint: Apply the link-back check and find the detail that cannot answer ‘How does this advance the focus?’
parts.correct_explanation: The lettering and shoes may be observable, but they do not help prove that dividing tasks supported management or adaptation.

parts.prompt: Which focus map best prepares the composition for E6.5?

options.text: Focus: the step-by-step method makes complex situations manageable and supports adaptation. Paragraph 1 job: show the initial task plan. Paragraph 2 job: show the same method during the rain disruption. Link-back: both moments show calm action on one clear part at a time.
Focus: school is useful. Paragraph jobs: mention every subject I can remember.
Focus: the charity sale. Paragraph jobs: describe food, music, clothing and decorations.
Focuses: planning and leadership. Paragraph jobs: switch to whichever one has more words available.

choice_rationales.A: The central response, distinct paragraph jobs and explicit evidence link all reinforce one focus.
choice_rationales.B: This focus is vague and the proposed list breaks the task's one-skill scope.
choice_rationales.C: Event description replaces the required explanation of transferred learning.
choice_rationales.D: Two competing centres prevent paragraph-level control.

parts.hint: Choose the map in which one central response controls two distinct paragraph jobs and both links can be explained.
parts.correct_explanation: The complete focus map supplies one claim, two non-overlapping contributions and a clear reason both pieces of evidence belong.
